```markdown
# Spec: Note pinning
Spec ID: SPEC-01
Status: draft
Supersedes: —

## Problem & user
A user of the notes API who keeps many notes has no way to keep the few they use most at hand: `GET /notes` returns every note in one undifferentiated list, so the important ones have to be found again on every visit. As the list grows, that search costs the user time on every request.

## Goals / Non-goals
**Goals**
- A user can mark up to 3 of their own notes as pinned and unmark them again.
- Pinned notes appear before all unpinned notes in `GET /notes`.

**Non-goals**
- Pinning another user's notes, or shared or global pins.
- A configurable pin limit (the limit is fixed at 3).
- Changing the order of unpinned notes.
- Folders, tags, favourites or any other grouping.

## User stories
- US-1: As a notes user, I want to pin a note, so that it appears at the top of my note list.
- US-2: As a notes user, I want to unpin a note, so that it returns to its normal position in the list.
- US-3: As a notes user, I want to be told when I have reached the pin limit, so that I know why a pin did not happen.

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)

### API — pin and unpin
- [ ] AC-1 WHEN the caller sends [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: route and method for pinning — e.g. `PUT /notes/:id/pin`? — OQ-1] for one of their own unpinned notes while they have fewer than 3 pinned notes, the API shall mark that note as pinned.
- [ ] AC-2 WHEN the caller sends [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: route and method for unpinning — e.g. `DELETE /notes/:id/pin`? — OQ-1] for one of their own pinned notes, the API shall mark that note as unpinned.
- [ ] AC-3 WHEN a note is unpinned, the API shall make that pin slot available for another note.
- [ ] AC-4 IF the caller attempts to pin a note while they already have 3 pinned notes, THEN the API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: reject the request with an error status, or unpin the oldest pin and accept? — OQ-2].
- [ ] AC-5 IF the note to pin or unpin does not exist or belongs to another user, THEN the API shall respond with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which status — `404` for both cases? — OQ-4] and change no pin state.
- [ ] AC-6 The API shall count at most 3 pinned notes per user at any time.
- [ ] AC-7 WHEN the caller pins a note that is already pinned, the API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: succeed without change, or return an error? — OQ-5].
- [ ] AC-8 The API shall limit pin state to the note's owner, so that pinning by one user never affects another user's `GET /notes` order.

### API — listing
- [ ] AC-9 The response of `GET /notes` shall list all of the caller's pinned notes before any unpinned note, ordered among themselves [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: by pin time, newest first, or by another key? — OQ-3].
- [ ] AC-10 Unpinned notes in the `GET /notes` response keep the same relative order they would have without this feature.
- [ ] AC-11 IF the caller has no pinned notes, THEN `GET /notes` shall return the same list, in the same order, as before this feature.
- [ ] AC-12 The response of `GET /notes` shall include every one of the caller's notes exactly once, whether or not it is pinned.

## Edge cases
- A pinned note is deleted via `DELETE /notes/:id`: it disappears from the list and no longer counts toward the limit (AC-3, AC-6).
- The caller pins the same note twice: it is still one pinned note (AC-7, AC-6).
- The caller unpins a note that is not pinned: no state change; the response is not decided, and follows the same answer as OQ-5.
- Two concurrent pin requests while the caller has 2 pinned notes: at most 3 notes end up pinned (AC-6).
- The caller has fewer than 3 notes in total: everything they have can be pinned (AC-1).

## Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: `GET /notes` p95 latency shall not increase by more than 10 ms compared with the same request before this feature, for a user with 1,000 notes.
- NFR-2: Every pin and unpin request shall be logged with the user ID, note ID, action and resulting pin count; note content shall not be logged.

## Inputs and provenance
**Data inputs**

| Input | Source | Trusted? | Freshness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Note ID in the pin or unpin request | API caller | No | Per request |
| Caller identity | Existing authentication of the API | Yes | Per request |
| Pin state and pin time of each note | Database | Yes | Current at read time |

**Requirement provenance**
- 3-pin limit, pinned-first listing in `GET /notes`: the request.
- `GET /notes` lists the caller's own notes; `DELETE /notes/:id` exists; there is no existing pin or update route: `src/notes/routes.ts:2-4`.
- Specs belong in `docs/specs/`: `AGENTS.md:3`.

## Untrusted inputs
- Note ID from the API caller. Threats: pinning or unpinning another user's note, probing which note IDs exist, and malformed IDs. Covered by AC-5 and AC-8; the exact response is open in OQ-4.

## Open questions
- OQ-1: What are the route and method for pin and unpin? — default if unanswered: `PUT /notes/:id/pin` and `DELETE /notes/:id/pin` — blocks: AC-1, AC-2
- OQ-2: What happens when pinning a 4th note? — default if unanswered: reject it with `409 Conflict`, without unpinning anything automatically — blocks: AC-4
- OQ-3: How are pinned notes ordered among themselves? — default if unanswered: most recently pinned first — blocks: AC-9
- OQ-4: What status is returned for a missing note or another user's note? — default if unanswered: `404` for both, so the API does not reveal that the note exists — blocks: AC-5
- OQ-5: Is pinning an already-pinned note (or unpinning an unpinned one) a success? — default if unanswered: yes, idempotent `200` with no state change — blocks: AC-7
- OQ-6: Does `GET /notes` expose each note's pin state? — default if unanswered: yes, a boolean `pinned` field on each note — blocks: none

## Changelog
- 2026-10-21 · draft — created — initial draft from the feature request.
```
